extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policymakers, patent/plant-variety office staff, researchers and analysts using WIPO plant variety and geographical indication statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological definitions for compiling, counting, and interpreting WIPO statistics on plant variety applications/titles and geographical indications, including counting conventions (absolute vs equivalent), residence classification, and data limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office data vs origin data
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data, whereas applications filed by applicants at a national or regional office (resident applications) or at foreign offices (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Origin of an application is determined by the residence of the applicant. Both office data and origin data are reported and used to complement each other (e.g., office volumes vs filing behaviour by applicant origin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident filing classification for CPVO (EU)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants domiciled in European Union (EU) member states, filing at the CPVO regional office is regarded as a resident filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification affects breakdowns of resident vs non-resident filings and the construction of origin data when regional offices (CPVO) are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute count vs Equivalent count (regional office treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute counts treat an application received by a regional office only once, while equivalent counts treat a single application filed at a regional office as equivalent to multiple applications (multiplied by the number of member states of the regional office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (CPVO): to compute equivalent applications in 2021, each CPVO application was multiplied by 27 member states; if the applicant resided in one of the 27 EU member states, the application was counted as one resident filing and 26 filings abroad; if the applicant did not reside in an EU member state, the application was counted as 27 filings abroad. The same methodology is applied to OAPI. Equivalent counts move countries that file intensively via regional offices up the ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent/absolute count ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: A ratio used to compare equivalent counts with absolute counts, indicating the multiplier effect of counting regional-office filings as multiple equivalent filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in tables (e.g., D13, D15) to show how much larger equivalent counts are compared to absolute counts; useful to interpret rankings and cross-country comparisons when regional office filings are significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs Non-resident share and contribution to growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics present the resident and non-resident share of filings and break down total growth into contributions from resident and non-resident applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures (e.g., D6) show how total growth in applications is decomposed: for example, Japan’s +8.8% growth in 2021 had resident applications contributing 2.4 percentage points and non-resident applications 6.4 percentage points. Use this decomposition to understand drivers of changes at each office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-lag caution: do not compare applications and titles in same year
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for issuing titles (grants/registrations) varies across offices and there can be processing capacity differences and procedural delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the time lag between filing and title issuance, data on applications for any given year should not be compared directly with data on titles issued that same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Geographical Indication (GI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication is a sign identifying a good as originating from a specific geographical area and possessing a given quality, reputation or other characteristic essentially attributable to that geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main function of a GI is to identify goods whose quality, reputation or other characteristics are strongly connected to the territory of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal means of protection for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs can be protected through a variety of legal means (e.g., sui generis systems, trademark laws, regional systems, international agreements, other national legal means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection of GIs at national level is often shared among several agencies. WIPO notes data-collection limitations: many countries are unable to identify GIs protected through the trademark system, which affects completeness of GI statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting GIs to minimize double counting (EU and Lisbon)
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize double counting, GIs in force through the European Union (EU) regional system and the Lisbon System are counted once only, rather than multiplied by the number of member states party to each system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with this convention, the overall total will inevitably include some double counting because GIs protected through bilateral, plurilateral or multilateral agreements could be included multiple times. Excluding GIs in force through various international agreements reduces the reported total substantially (example: ~63,600 total vs ~20,600 excluding international agreements).

rubrics_metrics.name: World totals are WIPO estimates (coverage notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals reported in charts and tables are WIPO estimates using data covering a specified number of offices (e.g., 71 offices for plant variety applications; 70 offices for some in-force totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note the scope of coverage when interpreting world totals and growth rates because not all national/regional authorities may have reported data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for missing or not-applicable data
rubrics_metrics.description: '..' indicates not available; 'n.a.' indicates not applicable. Footnotes (a), (b), (c) denote specific caveats (e.g., office did not report data; office not a UPOV member; different reporting conventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notations and footnotes must be checked in the statistical tables to understand incomplete series or special reporting circumstances that affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles in force: definition and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant variety titles in force is the count of active (granted/registered) plant variety titles at the end of the year; growth rates indicate year-on-year changes in the stock of active titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluctuations in titles in force can result from changes in processing capacity, procedural delays, renewals/expirations and differences in national procedures; interpret growth and levels with these factors in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of table-level notes and selection criteria (top offices/origins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charts and tables often select 'top' offices or origins based on 2021 totals or other criteria; notes explain selection (e.g., top five offices selected based on their 2021 totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing trend charts (e.g., top five offices 2000–2021), ensure you understand the basis for selection and any changes in coverage or membership (e.g., CPVO membership change due to UK withdrawal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation guidance for regional/regulatory changes (example: UK withdrawal from CPVO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in political/administrative arrangements (e.g., UK no longer a CPVO member in 2021) can shift filing patterns and classifications (resident/non-resident), affecting reported volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report explains specific impacts: UK filings rose +214.6% in 2021 because applicants must now file directly at the UK office rather than via CPVO, while CPVO resident filings dropped partly due to shifts in member-state origin reporting.
